newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-HANDS OFF DUNDEE, KARLSRUHE TELL BAYERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HANDS OFF DUNDEE, KARLSRUHE TELL BAYERN.

text.p: Karlsruhe warned Bundesliga leaders Bayern Munich on Wednesday not to try to poach striker Sean Dundee as a replacement for Juergen Klinsmann.
"Klinsmann's going to leave, I'm sure of that. And if Bayern come to get Sean, I'll get an allergy," Karlsruhe coach Winfried Schaefer told the Rheinpfalz newspaper.
South African-born Dundee, whose application to become a German citizen was approved on Tuesday, is the Bundesliga's leading scorer this season with 13 goals.

Schaefer has seen much of his home-grown talent move to Munich for big money over the last few years. Of the current Bayern squad, midfielder Mehmet Scholl, goalkeeper Oliver Kahn and defender Oliver Kreuzer all came from Karlsruhe.
"We need Sean Dundee here for us, because we're trying to build something of our own," Schaefer said.
Klinsmann has said he will leave Bayern at the end of the season unless they change the playing style adopted by coach Giovanni Trapattoni, which he says is too negative.
One newspaper even reported on Tuesday that Klinsmann had asked to be transferred immediately but the club had rejected his demand. Bayern have declined to comment on the report.

Dundee is expected to join Klinsmann in the national team soon, now that his application for citizenship has been approved. Press reports suggest he could make his debut in a friendly against Israel in February.
